title: Bridging Loan for Land with Planning
h1: Bridging Loan for Land with Planning (link title as indexed; not confirmed as on-page H1)
summary: Case study of a GBP 1.2 million bridging loan arranged by Silver Oak Capital on a development site in Glasgow. The site was valued at GBP 2 million WITHOUT planning consent (valuation by Knight Frank). The borrower was an offshore trust company that wanted to release value from its assets to fund the entire planning application for a proposed 220-unit residential scheme with ground-floor commercial space. Structure: GBP 1.2m loan, 60% LTV, 0.9% per month, 18-month term, interest rolled up. Challenges: unconsented land is hard to lend on (fewer lenders take 'planning risk') and the borrowers refused to give a personal guarantee; the deal was made possible by the borrowers' strong track record and experienced team. Lender identity/type, timing to completion and the later fate of the scheme are not revealed by the search results. Note: the page title says 'land with planning' but the body describes land valued without planning; both search summaries flag this inconsistency.
